newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance former CFO Doyle dies.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance former CFO Doyle dies.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co, the beleaguered auto financing company, said Friday its former chief financial officer, James Doyle died earlier this week.
Doyle was a central figure in January when the company said that it would have to restate its past four years' earnings due to accounting irregularities.
Mercury did not give the cause of death. A report in suburban Chicago Daily Herald on Friday said that Doyle died Wednesday evening of an apparent heart attack.
In January, Mercury said Doyle had disappeared.

But Doyle's attorney was later quoted in published reports saying Doyle had not disappeared, but was cooperating with federal officials. The Federal Bureau of Investigations in February searched Mercury's Lake Forest, Illinois headquarters seeking financial records.
In April, Mercury said it estimated on a preliminary basis that its net loss for 1996 was $48 million to $55 million.

Mercury has also defaulted on its commerical debt, but has received financing for day-to-day operations as William Brandt Jr., a bankruptcy and turnaround specialist who was brought in as chief executive officer in January, tries to mend the firm's fortunes.

"Mercury has come a long way from early 1997 and we are on the mend, but we wanted to take this moment to say that whatever the situation has been, we are saddened to hear about Jim Doyle's death," Brandt said in a news release.
Mercury shares were unchanged at 2-3/8 Friday.
